page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128gb is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. The system architecture is x86_64, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is network-attached, with a minimal local allocation of 1 GB.

In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression fall into the average tier (middle 50%). Memory performance is robust, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, while uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. For specialized workloads, the CPU supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and VNNI, which assist in low-latency tasks such as small-model LLM text generation, where it achieves top-tier throughput.

This hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive local storage or GPU acceleration. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a generous 128.0 GB RAM allocation makes it suitable for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, data processing pipelines, and moderate web serving. However, the reliance on network-attached storage and the lack of a dedicated GPU make it less suitable for heavy local I/O operations or large-scale deep learning training.
